editing: Idle time and native file dialogs are omitted. Prompt controls are shown before the save step. Other steps follow their recorded order. Instructions are burned into a separate caption area below the app. No narration.
prompt: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.

chapters.caption:
2 / Generate test input
Use Text tokens and GGUF embedded vocabulary (open model).

Choose the Pangram sample.
The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.

3 / Save and assign tokens
Leave sequence length blank. Use NT layout, int64, and npz.

Choose Generate, save & assign. Save bonsai27b-pangram.npz.
The generated tokens are assigned to the next trace.

4 / Review Trace settings
CPU NumPy decoder. Capture all 132 values within the chosen limits.

Choose Approve & run trace.
The worker runs a forward pass using the assigned prompt.

CPU inference in progress | 16x speed
This is a real run of the local 27B checkpoint.

Trace complete: 132 readable activations.
The Traced model view preserves the block connections.

5 / Search for logits. Click the output port below Language model head.
The green port opens the captured tensor.

The logits are float32 with shape (1, 10, 248320).
Each prompt position has one score per vocabulary entry.

6 / Inspect next-token predictions
At the last prompt position, token 271 has 28.00% probability.

Statistics shows the numerical distribution.
This capture contains no NaN or infinite values.

Visualization displays the captured activation layer.
The spatial preview is sampled for display.

Scroll down to the value distribution.
All captured finite values contribute to this histogram.
